help.people-at-work.title: Add people at the counter or on the floor
help.people-at-work.summary: The people who work a shop’s counter or a hub’s floor sign in as themselves, with their own phone and PIN, and what each of them does is kept under their name.
help.people-at-work.step1: The owner — signed in as the shop or the hub — opens People at the counter (Shop app) or People on the floor (Hub app) on the home screen, and adds a person by their phone number and the name they go by.
help.people-at-work.step2: They say yes from their own SeeBuyGet sign-in. Then, on the shop’s or the hub’s phone: “I work at the counter here” or “I work on the floor here”, with their number and their PIN.
help.people-at-work.step3: What they do is kept under their name, in “Who did what” in the same place. The fee, the money, the hours and the people stay with the owner: those are not shown to them, and refused if tried.
help.people-at-work.step4: Take somebody out and they are signed out at once, wherever they are signed in.
help.people-at-work.note1: A person’s PIN is theirs: never ask for it, and never share the owner’s password with the people who work for you.
help.risk-register.title: Corridors and hubs rated high risk
help.risk-register.summary: SeeBuyGet rates every corridor and hub low, medium or high for pilferage, hijacking, unrest and roadblock extortion, and looks at each rating again every quarter. Where something is rated high, parcels move only in bags closed on a coded seal, and nothing moves at night.
help.risk-register.step1: Below, every corridor and hub with its four ratings. “Rate” sets them, with why; “Still right” when a rating has come up for its quarterly look. Each is dated in your name.
help.risk-register.step2: A corridor rated high: a shop hands no loose parcel onto it — bag them, and close the bag on a coded seal — and nothing goes onto it between 19:00 and 06:00, on the clock where the shop or hub is.
help.risk-register.step3: A hub rated high: a bag leaves it only on a coded seal, and none is loaded there between 19:00 and 06:00. The hub is told in its bell when its rating changes, and so is a fleet that runs a corridor.
help.risk-register.note1: Shop app and Hub app: a refusal says which corridor or hub is rated high, for what, and what lets the parcels go — a bag on a seal, or the morning.
help.security-declaration.title: Sign the security declaration
help.security-declaration.summary: Every shop, hub, fleet and rider in no fleet signs a short security declaration: how they keep what is in their care. It is signed when they join and again every year. Without one in force, nothing new is taken on — what is already in their hands is finished as usual.
help.security-declaration.step1: Shop app, Hub app, Fleet app or Driver app: on the home screen, the declaration — a handful of promises. Read them and press “I declare this — sign”. It is signed in your name, today, for a year.
help.security-declaration.step2: A month before the year is up, the home screen says it runs out, and on what day. Sign it again then; nothing stops in the meantime.
help.security-declaration.step3: Not signed, or a year gone, or a new wording SeeBuyGet has written: a shop takes no parcel in, a hub opens no new tote, and a fleet’s drivers or a rider in no fleet take no new load, parcel or bag. Each refusal says where to sign.
help.security-declaration.note1: A fleet’s drivers sign nothing of their own: the fleet signs, and answers for them. At a shop, the owner signs — not the people at the counter.
help.new-partner-limit.title: The limit for a new shop or rider
help.new-partner-limit.summary: Where your country’s company has set one, a new shop holds at most so many parcels at once, and a new rider in no fleet carries at most so many. The limit grows with every parcel you hand on, and goes once you have handed on enough.
help.new-partner-limit.step1: Shop app: the home screen says how many parcels you hold, your limit now, and how it grows. At your limit a parcel is refused at take-in, and the screen says why.
help.new-partner-limit.step2: Driver app: My loads says how many parcels you carry and your limit now. At your limit a shop keeps the rest of the parcels for the next rider, and a load is not taken over until you have handed one on.
help.new-partner-limit.step3: Each parcel you hand on — to a driver, to the person who collects it, or delivered — raises your limit by one. After the number your company set, there is no limit at all.
help.new-partner-limit.step4: A bicycle or motorcycle rider in no fleet: until SeeBuyGet has seen a photo of your ID, your limit stays where it starts. Driver app, home screen: “Send a photo of your ID”. You are told when it has been seen — from then it grows as above — or why not, and you send another.
help.new-partner-limit.note1: A fleet’s drivers have no such limit: their fleet answers for them. Whether there is a limit, and its numbers, are your country’s company’s to set.
help.change-password.title: Change your password
help.change-password.summary: Change it whenever it may have been seen — you need the current one to do it.
help.change-password.step1: In the Shop or the Hub app: the round button at the top, then “Settings › Change your password”.
help.change-password.step2: Type your current password, then the new one twice. It needs at least 8 characters, and cannot be one that is easy to guess: a common word with a number on the end, your own name or email address, only digits, or a run like 12345678.
help.change-password.note1: Every other phone or computer still signed in with the old password is signed out at once. The one you used stays signed in.
help.change-password.note2: A wrong current password here counts like a wrong one at sign-in: five lock the account for a while.
help.change-password.note3: Changing the password, or resetting a forgotten one, turns off unlocking with a fingerprint or face on every phone of the shop or the hub. It can be turned on again under Settings.
help.fleet-code.title: Find your fleet code or issue a new one
help.fleet-code.summary: The code only names the fleet at sign-in. It never adds anyone to your fleet. Issue a new one if it has been shared with people who should no longer have it.
help.fleet-code.step1: Fleet app: “Dashboard › Fleet sign-in code”. Tap Show to read it.
help.fleet-code.step2: Tap “Issue a new code” and confirm. The old code stops working at once.
help.fleet-code.step3: Tell the other managers of your fleet the new code. Nobody is signed out: their phone and PIN still work.
help.fleet-code.note1: The card says when the code was last changed, and suggests a new one once it is over 90 days old.
help.fleet-roster.title: Take a driver on or off your fleet
help.fleet-roster.summary: You add a new driver yourself. A driver who is already on SeeBuyGet joins only when you offer them a place and they say yes.
help.fleet-roster.step1: New to SeeBuyGet: “Drivers › Onboard a driver”. Type their details and the phone number they will sign in with.
help.fleet-roster.step2: Already on SeeBuyGet: “Drivers › Offer a place to a driver already on SeeBuyGet”. Type the phone number they sign in with and tap Offer a place.
help.fleet-roster.step3: They see the offer in their driver app and say yes or no. Until they say yes, you see only the number you typed.
help.fleet-roster.step4: To take a driver off: “Drivers › Take off fleet” beside their name. Choose why; they are shown your reason.
help.fleet-roster.note1: An offer stays open for 7 days. You can take it back while it is open.
help.fleet-roster.note2: A driver carrying one of your loads, or rostered on one of your runs, cannot be taken off until the load is delivered or handed back and somebody else is on the run.
help.fleet-roster.note3: A driver you take off keeps their own trips, papers and rating. Every trip they did for you stays in your records.
help.fleet-roster.note4: Only your own drivers can start a shift on your vehicles.
help.fleet-roster.note5: You choose a driver’s vehicle under Shifts; it goes to the top of their list and they are told. The driver starts the shift themselves, with their PIN. Nobody starts a shift for somebody else.
help.fleet-roster.note6: A driver can also leave by themselves, from their own app, once their shift has ended and nothing is in their hands. You are told in the bell, with any of your runs that now have no driver. A run that has not left yet does not hold them: put somebody else on it.
help.driver-fleet.title: Join or leave a fleet
help.driver-fleet.summary: A fleet takes you on by offering you a place. You say yes or no in the app. No code is typed anywhere.
help.driver-fleet.step1: Give the fleet office the phone number you sign in with.
help.driver-fleet.step2: When they offer you a place, it shows on your home screen, and under your picture, then Your fleet.
help.driver-fleet.step3: Tap “Drive for” and the fleet’s name to say yes, or “No thanks”. Only you can answer, from your own sign-in.
help.driver-fleet.note1: You cannot say yes while you are on a shift, carrying a load, or rostered on a run of your current fleet. The app says what to finish first.
help.driver-fleet.note2: Your licence, trips and rating come with you. The fleet you leave keeps the trips you did for it.
help.driver-fleet.note3: If a fleet takes you off, the app says who and why. You cannot start a shift until another fleet offers you a place, or you choose to ride for yourself.
help.driver-fleet.note4: You can leave a fleet by yourself: your name at the top, then “Your fleet › Leave” and the company’s name. Nobody’s permission is needed. End your shift first, and deliver or hand back anything you are carrying; the app says what still stands in the way. Their office is told. If you are on one of their runs that has not left yet, you come off it. After you leave you cannot start a shift until a fleet offers you a place, or you choose to ride for yourself.
help.driver-fleet.note5: Your earnings screen says who was paid. In a fleet, the money goes to your fleet. In no fleet, it says that what you earned while you drove for one was paid to that fleet, and that nothing is owed to you for it. Money that reached you for work you did on your own is shown beside either.
help.driver-fleet.note6: Riding for yourself: when you are in no fleet and ride a bicycle or a motorcycle, Your fleet has “Ride for yourself”. Choose the country you live in — the app then names the company you would ride for — say which vehicle is yours and type its plate. It is done at once: the vehicle is on your start screen, and from then on you are paid directly. Your licence, trips and rating stay as they are. On a van, a truck or anything heavier than a motorcycle it is an ask: add a photograph of your ID card and of your driving licence (and a truck’s body), then “Ask to ride for myself”. Network staff read both and check your record; until they decide nothing changes, and Your fleet says the ask is waiting. You are told on your phone either way — if they say no, with their reason, and you may ask again.
help.close-account.title: Close your account
help.close-account.summary: A SeeBuyGet account that has gone four years without a sign-in can be closed by its owner. Nothing closes by itself.
help.close-account.step1: When your account has gone four years without a sign-in, we tell you in the app, and by email if you have a recovery email, that it can be closed.
help.close-account.step2: Tap your picture, then “Settings › Close my account”. In the Send app: “Account › Settings › Close my account”.
help.close-account.step3: If something is still open, it says what. When nothing is, type your PIN and tap “Close my account”.
help.close-account.note1: Closing cannot be undone. Your name, ID number, phone number, email and ID photos are removed, and you are signed out everywhere.
help.close-account.note2: Parcels, hand-overs and consignment notes stay, showing “closed account” where you were: they are other people’s records too.
help.close-account.note3: Your phone number is let go. It can sign up again, as a new account, and finds nothing of the old one.
help.close-account.note4: An account can be closed only once it has gone four years without a sign-in. Until then, you can rest it under “Settings › Mute my account”.
help.mute-account.title: Mute your account
help.mute-account.summary: Muting rests your SeeBuyGet account: nothing new reaches it until you unmute it, and nothing is deleted.
help.mute-account.step1: Tap your picture, then “Settings”. In the Send app: “Account › Settings”.
help.mute-account.step2: Tap “Mute my account”. It says what muting does; tap “Mute my account” again to do it.
help.mute-account.step3: To wake your account, open the same row — it now says “Unmute my account” — and tap “Unmute my account”.
help.mute-account.note1: While your account is muted, a shop of yours is not offered for new parcels and leaves the map, you are offered no loads as a driver, your fleet takes no new work, and your store takes no new orders. What you already hold goes on, and a sort hub keeps sorting what the network sends it.
help.mute-account.note2: Sign-in codes and messages about your account’s safety still reach you. Other notifications go to the list in the app without ringing your phone, and other emails are not sent.
help.mute-account.note3: Muting covers every role on your account at once: your account is your phone number, and your roles are what you do with it.
help.change-pin.title: Change your PIN
help.change-pin.summary: Your PIN is 5 digits. Change it with the current one — or, if you have forgotten it, with a code sent to your phone.
help.change-pin.step1: Driver and Fleet app: tap your picture, then “Settings › Change your PIN”.
help.change-pin.step2: Send app: “Account › Settings › Change your PIN”.
help.change-pin.step3: Forgot it? On the sign-in screen tap the forgot-PIN link. We send a code to your phone and you choose a new PIN.
help.change-pin.note1: Changing your PIN signs out every other phone that PIN had opened, in every app.
help.change-pin.note2: A PIN that is easy to guess is refused: mostly one digit, a run like 12345 or 13579, or a pattern like 12312.
help.change-pin.note3: A PIN is five digits, not four, so that it is not the same PIN as the one for your mobile money or your bank card. Do not use that one with a digit added.
help.change-pin.note4: A PIN replaced with a code — forgotten, or locked — works on the phone or browser you did it on. Every other one asks for a code again.
help.change-pin.note5: Replacing a forgotten PIN on a phone or browser you have not signed in on before asks for two codes: the one to your number, and one to the recovery email on your account. Type that email address and we send it a code. On a phone you have signed in on before, the code to your number is enough.
help.change-pin.note6: We write to your recovery email, and tell you in the app, whenever your PIN is replaced or starts working on a new phone or browser. If it was not you, replace your PIN straight away: that shuts out every other phone and browser.
help.change-pin.note7: “Settings › Phones and browsers” shows every phone and browser your PIN works on, with when each was confirmed and last used. “Forget all the others” asks for your PIN and signs you out everywhere; each of the others then needs a code to your number before your PIN works there again. On a phone or a computer that is not yours, use “Sign out, and forget this one”.
help.change-pin.note8: Changing your PIN, or replacing a forgotten one, turns off unlocking with your fingerprint or face on every phone. Turn it on again under Settings.
help.who-you-contract-with.title: Who you contract with
help.who-you-contract-with.summary: Settings shows the SeeBuyGet company you contract with and the licences and insurance it trades on, each with its number. If one is not right, you can say so.
help.who-you-contract-with.step1: Open “Settings › Who you contract with”. Shop, Hub, Driver, Fleet and Store app: tap your picture, then Settings. Business app: Settings.
help.who-you-contract-with.step2: Each licence and insurance policy shows what it is, its number, who issued it and until when it is good. Check the number with whoever issued it.
help.who-you-contract-with.step3: If one is not right, tap “This is not right”. Choose what is wrong, say it in your own words, and attach what shows it: a screenshot of the issuer’s register, or a photo.
help.who-you-contract-with.step4: Tap “Send the report”. Under the paper you will see that you reported it, and later what was decided and why.
help.who-you-contract-with.note1: Nothing changes by reporting. The paper keeps counting. The company is told what you said, never who said it, and has seven days to answer. Then SeeBuyGet staff decide: one of them can dismiss a report, and striking a paper takes two.
help.who-you-contract-with.note2: You see licences and insurance only. A company’s bank account, the people who may sign for it and the papers themselves are not shown.
help.who-you-contract-with.note3: The row is not there where no SeeBuyGet company contracts with you in your country.
help.store-secret.title: Rotate the signing secret
help.store-secret.summary: The secret signs every status update we send your shop system. It does not sign anybody in. Replace it whenever it may have been seen, or when you have lost it.
help.store-secret.step1: “My store › Signing secret › Rotate the secret”.
help.store-secret.step2: Type your password to confirm. A store with no email and password yet types the current secret instead.
help.store-secret.step3: The new secret is shown once. Save it before you close the sheet.
help.store-secret.step4: Update your shop system: updates we send from now on are signed with the new secret.
help.store-secret.note1: The card says when the secret was last changed, and suggests rotating it once it is over 90 days old.
help.store-secret.note2: A mistyped password here does not sign you out: the app says it was wrong and you try again.
help.store-secret.note3: Replacing the secret signs your store out on every other device.
help.api-keys.title: Make or replace a shipping API key
help.api-keys.summary: A publishable key can sit in your web page. A secret key belongs on your server only, and is shown once.
help.api-keys.step1: “My store › Shipping API keys › New key”.
help.api-keys.step2: Choose publishable or secret, and test or live.
help.api-keys.step3: Lost a secret key, or not sure who has it? Make a new one, switch to it, then revoke the old one.
help.api-keys.note1: Secret keys show how old they are, and suggest replacing one that is over 90 days old.
help.business-people.title: Add and remove people in your business
help.business-people.summary: An owner adds people by the phone number they sign in with. Nothing opens for them until they sign in themselves and say yes.
help.business-people.step1: “People › Add someone”: their phone number, their name, and what they may do.
help.business-people.step2: Owner: everything, including the people. Booker: the day-to-day work. Finance: the same, and the person your payments will be connected through. Viewer: sees everything, changes nothing.
help.business-people.step3: To take somebody out, press Remove on their row. It holds from their next click. Links to consignment notes that were emailed to them stop at the same moment.
help.business-people.step4: Leave takes you out of a business yourself. The only owner cannot leave until somebody else is an owner.
help.business-bell.title: Read the notices under the bell
help.business-bell.summary: What a carrier or SeeBuyGet tells your business is kept under the bell at the top of the Business app.
help.business-bell.step1: Tap the bell. The number on it is how many notices nobody in the business has read yet. The first is its welcome: what the bell tells you, and a tap on it opens “Get the most out of the app”.
help.business-bell.step2: Tap a notice. One about something of yours — a load, a booking, an export or an import, a contract offered to you — opens it at once and is marked read for everybody in the business, saying who read it. One that only says something opens in full.
help.business-bell.step3: A load opens on the part the notice is about: a problem on the way under On the road, a broken seal under Papers, a decided claim under Claim, and anything else on its Overview, where your answer is asked for. A booking opens under Runs, an export under Exports, an import under Imports.
help.business-bell.step4: Under a notice, “Mark as read” marks that one read without opening it, and “Show all” shows all of a long one. Mark all read clears the number in one go.
help.business-bell.note1: The inbox belongs to the business, not to you alone: everybody in the business reads the same one.
help.business-bell.note2: Somebody who can only view the business can read every notice but cannot mark one read. It stays unread until somebody who can act on it has read it.
help.business-bell.note3: Notices are not sent to a phone or a computer. Open the Business app to read them. Somebody taken out of the business stops seeing them straight away.
help.notices-bell.title: Read the notices under the bell
help.notices-bell.summary: What the network tells you is kept under the bell at the top of the app. A notice about something opens it in one tap.
help.notices-bell.step1: Tap the bell. The number on it is how many notices you have not read yet. The first is its welcome: what this bell tells you, and a tap on it opens “Get the most out of the app”.
help.notices-bell.step2: Tap a notice about something — a load, a chat, a parcel, an offer, your shift, your fleet — and it opens there at once, marked read. The notice says where it goes.
help.notices-bell.step3: A notice that only says something opens in full when you tap it. Under a notice, “Mark as read” marks it read without opening it, and “Show all” shows all of a long one.
help.notices-bell.note1: If you are driving, stop before you read the bell. Each notice is then one tap, and what it opens asks you to type nothing.
help.notices-bell.note2: Turned on for this device, notices also come to the phone while the app is closed. Tapping one there opens the same place.
help.business-loads.title: Post a load for carriers
help.business-loads.summary: Post a load for carriers on the open board, agree a price, and follow it to the door. You pay the carrier yourself.
help.business-loads.step1: “Domestic › Loads › Post a load”. It asks one part at a time. The bar at the top says which part you are on and what comes next, and that nothing goes public before the last step; Back takes you to the part before.
help.business-loads.step2: Who carries it, where there is a choice: the open board, or a carrier you have a contract with. Under a contract, say the day it must arrive, your order number and when it can be delivered — the carrier plans when it collects.
help.business-loads.step3: From and to: choose where it is collected and where it goes from your saved places — Save a new place adds one — or deliver to another business by the code it gave you. Say which country it goes to; across a border, who receives it and their address.
help.business-loads.step4: What it is: say what it is, what kind of goods, its weight, how it is packed and how many packages. Carriers read exactly this, and it goes on the consignment note. Dangerous goods are named as their safety data sheet names them: the UN number, the proper shipping name, the class and the packing group.
help.business-loads.step5: When it is collected — empty means as soon as a carrier can — then its value and how the price is set: carriers name their price and you accept one, or the first carrier at the board price takes it. Last, what the driver is told on the day, and who to ask for.
help.business-loads.step6: “Check and post” shows every part, and “Change” takes you back to one. It says who will see the load once it goes. “Post the load” puts it out — under a contract the button sends the order to your carrier — and shows you its code, with “Open the load” and “Post another”.
help.business-loads.step7: Open the load. Its record is in parts — “Overview”, “On the road”, “Papers”, “Payment” and “Claim” — tap a name, or swipe sideways. “Overview” has the prices offered, who is carrying it, the tracking link to share and the consignment note; “Papers” has the links to the note.
help.business-loads.note1: SeeBuyGet does not take, hold or send the money for your loads. You pay the carrier directly, or through your own payment system.
help.business-loads.note2: You are told under the bell when a load is delivered, with who received it.
help.business-exports.title: Send a container out through a port
help.business-exports.summary: Record the booking your forwarder or the shipping line confirmed, and SeeBuyGet carries the road to the terminal before the gate closes: the empty out, the loaded box in, its weight, its seal, its papers and the box’s free days, with your clearing agent beside you — and one file for your forwarder at the gate. SeeBuyGet books no ship.
help.business-exports.step1: “Exports › Record an export by sea”. Copy the booking off its confirmation: the booking number and who it is with, the vessel and voyage, the gate-in, verified gross mass and documents cut-offs (in UTC), the empty release number. Choose where the box is stuffed, the terminal, and the depot if you fetch the empty yourself.
help.business-exports.step2: Under the export, one line says by when the loaded box must leave to be inside the gate before the cut-off — the road at a truck’s speed, with time to queue at the gate. You are told under the bell six hours before that time, if the gate closes without the box, and twelve hours before the verified gross mass cut-off while none is declared.
help.business-exports.step3: “Post the empty run” if you fetch the empty, write the box’s number, and declare its verified gross mass with who signs for it. Then “Post the load to the terminal”: a driver sees the gate cut-off and your booking. Write the seal on that load under Domestic › Loads, with its three photographs, before the driver collects it.
help.business-exports.step4: Give the papers under “The papers”: upload a file on its line, attach one of your documents, or write its reference — the export entry is the number your clearing agent gives you. Three groups: needed on every export (commercial invoice, packing list, export entry, and your letter of instruction); asked for these goods — put a paper on the list when the goods, the buyer or the border need it (a certificate of origin, a phytosanitary or health certificate, an export permit, an insurance certificate, any other by its name; hazardous goods carry their dangerous goods declaration from the start); and kept with the export when there is one (the booking confirmation, the weighbridge ticket, the bill of lading). Your packing list comes from your own file under “Packing list”: upload the workbook or file your system exports, or paste its cells — each column is read by its heading, any you match by hand is remembered for your next file, columns of your own are kept, and a line that cannot be read is shown by its row; then sign it. Your commercial invoice is drawn from the same lines under “Commercial invoice” — its prices and origins read from the same file (a unit price or value column, a country of origin): fill in its number, currency and buyer, add what the destination asks for besides (particulars by their own names, declarations in its own words, columns of your list), and sign it; what it carried is remembered for your next invoice to that country. Your letter of instruction to the forwarder is a form under “Shipper’s letter of instruction”: most of it comes from the export, and its goods from your packing list; fill in the consignee, who is notified, the port of discharge, the trade term, freight prepaid or collect, how the bill of lading is released and the goods lines, then sign it. Signed, it is kept exactly as signed — a change is a new version, and if the export changes under it (the weight, the box) you are asked to sign again. “Open the handover file” for your forwarder: what is still missing is marked in it. Once the forwarder issues the bill of lading, write its number on the export.
help.business-exports.step5: Under “The box’s clock”, write the free days the line gives — outside the terminal (detention), from the empty leaving the depot until the box is inside the gate, and inside it (demurrage), from the gate until it is loaded on board. The clock counts to a date and you are told under the bell three days before it, and once if it passes. Our driver’s collection of the empty starts it; if the line or your forwarder brought the empty, write when it left the depot. Once your forwarder says it is on the ship, write when it was loaded: the clock stops. If the box is your own (not lent by the line), say so — tick it when you record the export, or “The box is ours” — and no line’s clock runs on it.
help.business-exports.step6: “Clearing agent › Choose a clearing agent” to appoint one from the agents’ list. It is told, reads the papers attached on this export — not your other papers — gives the export entry, and accepts each paper or sends it back with a reason; a paper sent back shows as missing until you give it again. “End the appointment” when you are done: it stops reading at once, and is told. Its fee comes as a quotation under “Its fee”: agree to it there if it is the figure you agreed; either of you says when it is paid, with its reference. SeeBuyGet moves no money between you.
help.business-exports.note1: The verified gross mass is your declaration, handed to your forwarder: they declare it to the line. A box is not loaded on a ship without one.
help.business-exports.note2: SeeBuyGet carries the road and keeps the papers ready. The ocean leg, its booking and the bill of lading are your forwarder’s or the line’s; nothing is booked, filed or sent to a line from here, so any forwarder works with it.
help.business-exports.note3: A clearing agent finds the exports it was appointed on under its own Exports: open each paper, accept it or send it back, and give the export entry by its number. Put on the list what this border asks for these goods: the exporter is told. Quote your fee under “Its fee”: the exporter is told and agrees to it, and a new figure asks it to agree again. The free days are in the exporter’s agreement with the line: SeeBuyGet counts days, and never what a day over costs.
